item.title: “Householder, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in those forms,…
item.description:
“Householder, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in those forms, praises them, and dwells with lust for them, depending on them, consciousness arises with clinging to them. Householder, a monk who has clinging does not attain complete Nibbāna … Households, there are tastes cognizable by the tongue … Householder, there are phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable … enticing. If a monk delights in those phenomena, praises them, and dwells with lust for them — because he delights, praises, and dwells with lust, depending on them, consciousness arises with clinging to them. Having clinging, householder, that monk does not attain Nibbāna. This, householder, is the cause, this is the reason why some beings here and now do not attain complete Nibbāna.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.124

item.title: “Here, monks, the third kind of ascetics and brahmins think: ‘Those first ascetics and brahmins … have not escaped Māra’s power. Suppose we make a…
item.description:
“Here, monks, the third kind of ascetics and brahmins think: ‘Those first ascetics and brahmins … have not escaped Māra’s power. Suppose we make a hiding place near the bait cast by Māra and the world’s offerings. Having made a hiding place, without entering, without indulging, we will eat the bait and the world’s offerings. By not entering, not indulging, we will not become infatuated; not infatuated, we will not become heedless; not heedless, we will not become subject to Māra’s will among that bait and offerings.’ These ascetics and brahmins make a hiding place near the bait and offerings. Having done so, without entering, without indulging, they eat the bait and offerings. Not entering, not indulging, they do not become infatuated; not infatuated, they do not become heedless; not heedless, they do not become subject to Māra’s will. But then they have such wrong views as: ‘The world is eternal; the world is not eternal; the world is finite; the world is infinite …’ Thus, monks, these third ascetics and brahmins have not escaped Māra’s power.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 25 – Nivāpasutta

item.title: - What gives birth to a person? What always runs about? What undergoes rebirth? What does a person rely on? - Craving gives birth to…
item.description:
- What gives birth to a person?
What always runs about?
What undergoes rebirth?
What does a person rely on?
- Craving gives birth to a person,
The mind itself always runs about,
Beings undergo rebirth,
Kamma is what a person relies on.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.57

item.title: “Great king, there are three things in the world which, when they arise, lead to harm, suffering, and discomfort. What three? Great king, greed is…
item.description:
“Great king, there are three things in the world which, when they arise, lead to harm, suffering, and discomfort. What three? Great king, greed is a thing in the world which, when it arises, leads to harm, suffering, and discomfort. Great king, hatred is a thing in the world which, when it arises, leads to harm, suffering, and discomfort. Great king, delusion is a thing in the world which, when it arises, leads to harm, suffering, and discomfort. These three things in the world, when they arise, bring harm, suffering, and discomfort.

Greed, hatred, delusion — these three,
Are evil minds for a person,
They damage one’s own self,
They produce one’s own self,
Like the rind and core of a tree,
Producing its own fruit.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 3.23

item.title: Bemused by wealth and sensual pleasures, People are greedy and deluded, In the midst of sensual pleasures, Without clear awareness, They are overly intoxicated, Like…
item.description:
Bemused by wealth and sensual pleasures,
People are greedy and deluded,
In the midst of sensual pleasures,
Without clear awareness,
They are overly intoxicated,
Like a fish unaware of the trap set —
Later they suffer,
Experiencing the results of evil deeds.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 3.7

item.title: “What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the condition for the purification of beings?” “Mahāli, if form were exclusively happiness, immersed in happiness, accompanied…
item.description:
“What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the condition for the purification of beings?” “Mahāli, if form were exclusively happiness, immersed in happiness, accompanied by happiness, not accompanied by suffering, beings would not become disenchanted with form. But because form is suffering, Mahāli, immersed in suffering, accompanied by suffering, not accompanied by happiness, beings become disenchanted with form. Through disenchantment, they become dispassionate; through dispassion, they are liberated. This, Mahāli, is the cause, this is the condition for the purification of beings. Such being the cause, such being the condition, beings are purified. If feeling … perception … formations … if consciousness were exclusively happiness … beings would not become disenchanted with consciousness. But because consciousness is suffering … beings become disenchanted with consciousness … and are liberated. This, Mahāli, is the cause, this is the condition for the purification of beings.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.60

item.title: Elder Abhaya (2): “Seeing a form, mindfulness is lost — Attending to a pleasing sign, The mind feels infatuation, Clinging to the perception remains. The…
item.description:
Elder Abhaya (2):
“Seeing a form, mindfulness is lost —
Attending to a pleasing sign,
The mind feels infatuation,
Clinging to the perception remains.
The defilements increase,
Leading to the root of existence.”

From: Theragāthā 1.98

item.title: “Mind precedes all mental states, Mind is their chief; they are all mind-made. If with an impure mind one speaks or acts, Suffering follows like…
item.description:
“Mind precedes all mental states,
Mind is their chief; they are all mind-made.
If with an impure mind one speaks or acts,
Suffering follows like the wheel that follows the ox’s foot.”

“Mind precedes all mental states,
Mind is their chief; they are all mind-made.
If with a pure mind one speaks or acts,
Happiness follows like a shadow that never leaves.”

From: Dhammapada 1-20

item.title: “Monks, these five perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, ending in the deathless. What five? The…
item.description:
“Monks, these five perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, ending in the deathless. What five? The perception of impermanence, the perception of not-self, the perception of death, the perception of disgust with food, the perception of non-delight in the entire world. These five perceptions, monks, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, ending in the deathless.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.62

item.title: “What is wandering without a standing place? The bondage of standing and clinging to the sign of forms, householder, has been abandoned by the Tathāgata,…
item.description:
“What is wandering without a standing place? The bondage of standing and clinging to the sign of forms, householder, has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, made non-existent, so that it cannot arise again in the future. Therefore, the Tathāgata is called ‘one who wanders without a standing place.’ The bondage of standing and clinging to the sign of sounds … smells … tastes … touches … phenomena, householder, has been abandoned by the Tathāgata … Therefore, the Tathāgata is called ‘one who wanders without a standing place.’ Thus, householder, is wandering without a standing place.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.3
